| # | Feature | What it should do | Your example |
|---|---|---|---|
| 14.1 | Abstract | Write the beginning of a short paper with a title, an author line, and an abstract set apart from the body. | `	itle{On Sorting}
\author{A. Smith}
\maketitle
 egin{abstract}
We study the cost of sorting.
\end{abstract}` |
| 14.2 | Title block with affiliations and keywords | Write a paper's title block with two authors, each with a university affiliation, and a list of keywords. | `	itle{On Sorting}
\author[1]{Ann Lee}
\author[2]{Bo Chen}
\affil[1]{University of Oxford}
\affil[2]{Stanford University}
\maketitle
	extbf{Keywords:} sorting, complexity, algorithms` |
| 14.3 | Theorem and proof | Write a short mathematical passage with a numbered theorem followed by its proof, ending with an end-of-proof mark. | ` egin{theorem}
There are infinitely many primes.
\end{theorem}
 egin{proof}
Suppose $p_1,\dots,p_n$ were all of them. Then $p_1\cdots p_n+1$ has a prime factor not in the list, a contradiction.
\end{proof}` |
| 14.4 | Numbered definition | Write a numbered definition of a prime number, set apart from the surrounding text the way math books do. | ` egin{definition}
A \emph{prime number} is an integer $p>1$ whose only positive divisors are $1$ and $p$.
\end{definition}` |
| 14.5 | Epigraph | Write the opening of a chapter with a short epigraph quotation and its attribution, set apart before the first paragraph. | `\chapter{Beginnings}
\epigraph{All happy families are alike.}{Leo Tolstoy}
The story begins on a quiet morning.` |
| 14.6 | Pull quote | Write a paragraph of an article and a pull quote that repeats a striking line from it in larger type. | `The city never slept, and neither did its engineers. Every night the grid held by a thread.
\pullquote{Every night the grid held by a thread.}` |
| 14.7 | Framed box | Write a paragraph followed by a short piece of text inside a framed box. | `This is an ordinary paragraph of body text.
 box{\parbox{0.8	extwidth}{	extbf{Note:} Save your work before continuing.}}` |
| 14.8 | Algorithm in pseudocode | Write a short algorithm in numbered pseudocode with the caption 'Binary search'. | ` egin{algorithm}
\caption{Binary search}
 egin{algorithmic}[1]
\State $lo \gets 0$, $hi \gets n-1$
\While{$lo \le hi$}
\State $mid \gets \lfloor (lo+hi)/2 floor$
\If{$A[mid]=x$} \Return $mid$
\ElsIf{$A[mid]<x$} \State $lo \gets mid+1$
\Else \State $hi \gets mid-1$
\EndIf
\EndWhile
\State \Return $-1$
\end{algorithmic}
\end{algorithm}` |
| 14.9 | Subfigures | Write a passage with two images shown side by side, each with its own sub-caption (a) and (b), and one overall caption. | ` egin{figure}
\centering
 egin{subfigure}{0.45	extwidth}\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{a.png}\caption{Before}\end{subfigure}\hfill
 egin{subfigure}{0.45	extwidth}\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{b.png}\caption{After}\end{subfigure}
\caption{Results of the treatment.}
\end{figure}` |
| 14.10 | Reference to a page number | Write a sentence that refers to the page number where the section called Results begins, so the number updates automatically. | `\section{Results}\label{sec:results}
...
The findings are discussed on page~\pageref{sec:results}.` |
| 14.11 | List of figures | Write a short document outline that includes an automatically generated list of figures. | `	ableofcontents
\listoffigures
\section{Introduction}
\section{Methods}` |
| 14.12 | Appendix | Write a short document with two main sections followed by an appendix labeled with a letter. | `\section{Introduction}
\section{Methods}
\appendix
\section{Additional Proofs}` |
| 14.13 | Acronyms spelled out on first use | Write two sentences that use the acronym API, so that its first use is spelled out automatically and it appears in a generated list of acronyms. | `
ewacronym{api}{API}{application programming interface}
The \gls{api} exposes our data. A second call to the \gls{api} returns JSON.
\printglossary[type=\acronymtype]` |
| 14.14 | Units and quantities | Write a sentence giving a speed of 3.5 × 10^8 meters per second and a temperature of 21 degrees Celsius, with the units typeset correctly. | `The probe travelled at \SI{3.5e8}{\meter\per\second} in a room held at \SI{21}{\celsius}.` |
| 14.15 | Chemical equation | Write the balanced chemical equation for burning methane, typeset as chemistry. | `\ce{CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O}` |
| 14.16 | Margin to-do note | Write a paragraph with an editorial to-do note attached to it, shown in the margin. | `The experiment was repeated three times with similar results.	odo{Add citation for the replication study.}` |
| 14.17 | Line numbers for review | Write a short paragraph set up so that the printed version shows line numbers in the margin for reviewers. | `\usepackage{lineno}
\linenumbers
This paragraph will appear with line numbers in the margin so reviewers can refer to specific lines.` |
| 14.18 | Drop cap | Write the first paragraph of a story with its first letter set as a large drop cap. | `\lettrine{I}{t} was a dark and stormy night, and the old lighthouse keeper had not slept in days.` |
| 14.19 | Hyphenation hints | Write a sentence containing the word electroencephalography, marking the places where it may be hyphenated. | `The technician reviewed the elec\-tro\-en\-ceph\-a\-log\-ra\-phy results.` |
| 14.20 | Numbered paragraphs | Write three paragraphs of a contract that are numbered 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3 automatically. | ` egin{enumerate}[label=1.\arabic*]
\item The Supplier shall deliver the goods by the agreed date.
\item The Customer shall pay within thirty days of invoice.
\item Either party may terminate with written notice.
\end{enumerate}` |
| 14.21 | Colored text | Write a sentence where the word 'blocked' is shown in red text. | `The deployment is 	extcolor{red}{blocked} until the review is complete.` |
| 14.22 | Subtext line | Write a heading followed by a line of small, muted subtext under it. | `\section{Quarterly Report}
{\small\color{gray} Prepared by the finance team}` |
| 14.23 | Inline badge | Write a sentence ending with a small colored badge that reads 'beta'. | `The new search feature is now available \colorbox{orange}{	extcolor{white}{\scriptsize beta}}` |
| 14.24 | Inline data fields | Write a note about a book that includes a rating of 5 and a genre of mystery as data fields a query tool could read. | `Finished reading *The Big Sleep*. [rating:: 5] [genre:: mystery]` |
| 14.25 | Key-value list | Write a short list of facts about a person (name, year born, occupation) that should display as aligned key-value pairs. | ` egin{description}
\item[Name] Ada Lovelace
\item[Born] 1815
\item[Occupation] Mathematician
\end{description}` |
| 14.26 | Side-brace grouping | Write three related lines grouped together by a large curly brace with a label beside it. | `$\left. egin{array}{l}x=1\y=2\z=3\end{array}ight\}\ 	ext{initial values}$` |
| 14.27 | Table formula | Write a small table of expenses whose total row is computed by a formula. | `\| Item \| Cost \|
\|------+------\|
\| Rent \| 1000 \|
\| Food \| 300 \|
\| Total \| \|
#+TBLFM: @4$2=vsum(@2..@3)` |
| 14.28 | Callout on one list item | Write a bulleted list where one item is highlighted as a warning by a marker at the start of that item. | `- Install the dependencies
- [!warning] Do not run this on production
- Run the tests` |
| 14.29 | Note template | Write a daily-note template that inserts today's date and the note's title automatically when a note is created. | `# <% tp.file.title %>
Date: <% tp.date.now("YYYY-MM-DD") %>

## Tasks
- [ ] ` |
| 14.30 | Inline icon | Write a sentence with a small heart icon from an icon set shown inline. | `We  aHeart\ open source software.` |
